source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Geography Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Locating Places — The Globe and the Grid
points: A **globe** is a true model of the Earth; a **map** is a flat drawing of the Earth or part of it.
To locate any place we use a grid of **latitudes** and **longitudes**.
**Latitudes** run **east–west** (parallel lines); **longitudes** (meridians) run **north–south** (from pole to pole).

sections.heading: 2. Latitudes (Parallels)
points: The **Equator** = 0° latitude; the longest latitude; divides Earth into **Northern** and **Southern** hemispheres.
Latitudes are measured from 0° to **90°** north and south.
Latitude affects **climate/heat zones**.

sections.heading: 3. Longitudes (Meridians)
points: The **Prime Meridian** = 0° longitude, passing through **Greenwich** (London).
Longitudes run from 0° to **180°** east and west; the two meet on the other side of the globe.
Longitude is linked to **time**: the Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours → **15° = 1 hour** (4 minutes per degree).
**GMT** (Greenwich Mean Time) is the world's reference time; **IST** (Indian Standard Time) is based on **82½° E** and is **5½ hours ahead of GMT**.

sections.heading: 4. Heat Zones of the Earth
points: **Torrid Zone** — between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn; receives the most direct sunlight (hottest).
**Temperate Zones** — between the tropics and the polar circles (moderate).
**Frigid Zones** — between the polar circles and the poles (coldest).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Equator = 0° latitude (longest); Prime Meridian = 0° longitude (Greenwich).
Latitudes run east–west; longitudes run north–south (pole to pole).
Tropic of Cancer = 23½° N (through India); Capricorn = 23½° S.
Arctic Circle = 66½° N; Antarctic = 66½° S; Poles = 90°.
15° longitude = 1 hour; IST = 82½° E, GMT + 5½ hours.
Heat zones: Torrid (hottest) → Temperate → Frigid (coldest).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Latitudes** run east–west but **measure** north–south distance; **longitudes** run north–south but measure east–west — don't confuse direction of the line with what it measures.
The **Tropic of Cancer (23½° N)** passes through India, not the Tropic of Capricorn.
Prime Meridian passes through **Greenwich**; IST reference longitude is **82½° E**.
Torrid Zone is the **hottest** (most direct sun), Frigid the **coldest**.
